findings.reason: Verified in the diff that every batch in CleanAnnotations and CleanOrphanedAnnotationTags calls r.log.Error unconditionally, so a healthy instance logs Error lines with count 0 on every cleanup cycle, and the lines carry the full ID slice; this is a real noise and alerting defect.

Confirmed cleanup.go:77 now ticks every minute while clean() still uses a 9-minute timeout and runs all eight cleanup jobs synchronously, so this unrelated ticker change increases DB load across every job with no stated reason.

The string concatenation is quadratic and the claim about multi-GB copying is plausible, but the branch only runs for SQLite with cleanupjob_batchsize above 999, while the default is 100, so it is a niche configured path.

Verified that t.Cleanup now wipes annotation and annotation_tag after each subtest and each subtest reseeds, so the 'run the delete again' case no longer tests a second run over cleaned data; the misleading name is a test-quality concern, not a product defect.
